repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR uses a rising-edge wait (`wait(MotionSensor.Motion == true, edge rising)`) which requires blocking until the predicate transitions from false to true. The candidate uses a periodic `if` check that only evaluates at the start of the 1s cycle period. Evidence F1 shows the motion state changed to true at t=100ms, but F2 shows no action was emitted because the candidate's `if` guard at t=0 was false and it did not wait for the rising edge.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with a blocking rising-edge wait state machine (`if (fired) { wait until(not C); fired=false }`, `wait until(C)`, BODY, `fired=true`). This ensures the action fires immediately upon the transition detected at t=100ms, matching the IR's rising-edge semantics. The period remains 1000 to match the IR's 1 SEC cycle period.
